node.label: Philip J Deloria
node.date_label: Playing Indian (1998) · Indians in Unexpected Places (2004) · Becoming Mary Sully: Toward an American Indian Abstract (2019)
node.description: A historian of American Indian peoples, representation and modernity. His selected bibliography includes Playing Indian, Indians in Unexpected Places and the recovery of artist Mary Sully’s work. In the publisher’s 2024 written Q&A he rejects a categorical separation of Indigenous people from modernity while describing Sully’s distinctive artistic position. The same account explains how family preservation, research, public talks and curatorial questions helped turn overlooked drawings into a historical argument and exhibitions; that collaboration does not make him the artwork’s author.
node.representative_figures_and_works: Playing Indian (1998); Indians in Unexpected Places (2004); Becoming Mary Sully: Toward an American Indian Abstract (2019). American Studies: A User’s Guide (2017) is coauthored with Alexander I. Olson and not reassigned as a sole work.
